chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Washa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, fasting is not merely from food and drink alone.'
Indeed, Maryam (peace be upon her) said: 'Surely I have vowed a fast to the Beneficent,' i.e., silence.
Therefore, preserve your tongues, and lower your gaze, and do not envy one another, and do not dispute.
For indeed, envy consumes faith just as fire consumes firewood.
ai.seo_question: What is the deeper meaning of fasting beyond abstaining from food and drink in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that true fasting transcends mere physical abstinence, integrating the spiritual discipline of *samt* (silence) as exemplified by Maryam’s vow in Surah Maryam. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab al-saum* (etiquettes of fasting), warning that envy and verbal disputes erode the essence of worship, much like fire consumes fuel. The reference to Maryam highlights the prophetic lineage of fasting as a holistic state of being, connecting physical restraint with inner tranquility and moral integrity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Washa, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The Fasts are not from the food and the drink alone.
Maryamas said [19:26] Surely I have vowed a fast to the Beneficent, i.e., silence.
Therefore, preserve your tongues, and lower your gaze, and neither envy nor dispute,
for the envy consumes the faith just as the fire consumes the firewood’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Washsha’ from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Fasting is not abstaining from food and drink only.
Mary had said, “I have made a vow before the Beneficent to fast,” meaning thereby to remain silent.
You must control your tongues and cast down your eyes. You must not be jealous and you must not quarrel.
Jealousy consumes belief just as fire consumes fire wood.’”
